title: Sparsity of a sampled Fourier polynomial
statement: Let $n,s$ be natural numbers, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and choose a set of coordinates $S_i$ for each $i mod s$. The number of nonzero Fourier coefficients of the Fourier polynomial formed from the distinct sampled sets $S_i$ is at most $s$.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued function on the n-dimensional sign cube
A choice of a set of coordinates for each of the s sample indices
